newsitem.title: USA: Eleven killed in storm-related accidents in Texas.
newsitem.headline: Eleven killed in storm-related accidents in Texas.

text.p: Eleven people were killed in weather-related traffic accidents in Texas after a severe winter storm swept across the state over the weekend and iced over highways and bridges, officials said on Tuesday.
"We have reports of 11 dead. That's from reports of accidents investigated by (state police)," said Sherri Deatherage Green, spokeswoman with the Texas Department of Public Safety.

Dozens of travelers remained stuck in a Houston Greyhound bus station waiting for highways to clear, and lawmakers struggled to make their way to the state capital in Austin for the opening session of the state legislature.

The winter storm had virtually paralysed much of Texas and Louisiana over the weekend. On Tuesday, ice that had accumulated on skyscrapers in downtown Houston crashed onto the streets and sent pedestrians scurrying for cover.
Managers of high-rise buildings roped off sidewalks and plazas to protect passersby in the business district from the falling ice.
"I keep thinking someone is knocking on the building here, and it's just ice hitting the side," meteorologist Mark Miles said. "This is one of the more severe storms we've seen in this region."
Utility crews in Houston were working to restore power to 50,500 customers who have been without electricity since Monday when ice-coated tree limbs fell across power lines.

"We're telling our customers that everybody should be back up at 8 o'clock tonight, 10 o'clock at the latest," Houston Lighting & Power Co. spokeswoman Leticia Lowe said. "The weather's really helped us out today."

A warming trend was expected to continue into the weekend, meteorologists said, melting off the heavy coating of ice that blanketed the city and closed schools and some businesses for a second straight day on Tuesday.
